title: Equendito
summary: Equendito is Tooker's recorded placename for Barren Island in Flatlands, Kings County. A 1664 deed identified the island by its Indigenous name and by the English name Broken Lands.
address_label: Historic Barren Island / Floyd Bennett Field area, Flatlands, Brooklyn, NY
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Equendito, Barren Island, and Broken Lands. The name is interpreted Equendito as land opened or broken up, land cleared of trees and brush for planting, matching the English and Dutch description Broken Lands.

Why Place Names Matter

“The name of a place tells the story of the people who live there.”

— TextProject, Stories of Words: Toponyms (2018), Our Changing Language, PDF page 19

Place-name history should show Native people as active and present, not only as names in old documents.
land_loss_content: Equendito preserves an Indigenous name for a Brooklyn island whose landscape was later renamed, reshaped, and absorbed into modern urban infrastructure. The 1664 deed language keeps visible both Indigenous proprietorship and the way colonial records translated Native land descriptions into English place labels.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker associates Equendito with historic Barren Island, now connected with Floyd Bennett Field and Jamaica Bay. Shoreline change, landfill, and development make its exact historic location uncertain.
